publication: Jean Gallier, Logic for Computer Science: Foundations of Automatic Theorem Proving, Chapter 8, Resolution in First-Order Logic (chapter excerpt; edition of the inspected excerpt not established).

reviews.checked_passages: Chapter 8 excerpt, §§8.4–8.5, especially definitions and separating renamings in §8.5.1, completeness and one-step lifting Lemma 8.5.3, refutation lifting Lemma 8.5.4, and Theorem 8.5.1 (printed pp. 395–404). Primary PDF text inspected; the author's book page confirms the corrected Dover second edition of June 2015, but the separate excerpt's edition was not established.
reviews.consumers: First-order resolution: factoring and lifting ground proofs.
reviews.outcome: The corpus uses finite proof trees, avoiding a graph-theory prerequisite. It uses two explicit disjoint injections of natural-number variables for each inference, rather than treating two bijections of the entire infinite variable set as disjoint. The most-general unifier factors arbitrary ground substitutions using the preceding term-unification result. Multi-literal removal/factoring is included explicitly; binary single-pair resolution is not silently treated as complete. Equality is handled by the separately proved congruence-axiom translation, with no paramodulation claim. No new serious defect in the adopted lifting argument was established.
